title: Omni Agent Capability Scorecard
description: Fixed baseline for judging capability maturity against Claude Code, Hermes, and OpenClaw reference surfaces.

capabilities.title: Local coding runtime
capabilities.referenceStrength: Claude Code has deeper terminal UX, recovery, and interactive tool presentation.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add richer CLI slash commands and run recovery flows that can replay persisted tool presentations across resumed sessions.
matureCriteria: CLI supports recovery-oriented coding sessions with structured tool output and operator-facing run state.
Failure repair and run recovery are covered by local benchmark scenarios and targeted tests.
blockedBy: Richer terminal UX and replayable tool presentation still trail claudecode-source.
Run recovery is CLI and artifact based; interactive recovery UX remains thinner than the reference.

capabilities.title: Shell and file safety
capabilities.referenceStrength: Claude Code and Hermes have deeper command, approval, and path-boundary governance.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Broaden command parsing regressions around shell aliases, wrappers, and platform-specific destructive forms.
matureCriteria: Shell and file tools fail closed across destructive, cross-shell, path-escape, and platform-specific command shapes.
Approval reasons, command rule ids, and resolved paths are observable in tests and operator output.
blockedBy: Shell parsing still needs broader shell alias and quoting coverage.
Operator-facing approval recovery remains CLI-oriented rather than a richer workbench flow.

capabilities.title: Memory lifecycle
capabilities.referenceStrength: Hermes has stronger provider lifecycle, review, and long-running memory behavior.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add deeper recall precision attribution and long-running memory review fixtures before marking mature.
matureCriteria: Memory recall is source-attributed, usefulness-scored, and able to reject stale or conflicting facts.
Provider lifecycle failures are visible and recoverable across long-running sessions.
blockedBy: Long-running memory review and recall precision fixtures are still limited.
No live or contract matrix proves provider lifecycle parity with hermes-agent-main.

capabilities.title: Skill lifecycle
capabilities.referenceStrength: Hermes has full skill create, patch, write file, remove file, review, and sync flows.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add richer revision history and remote skill sync before marking mature.
matureCriteria: Skill create, patch, support-file write/remove, review, promotion, rollback, and disable flows are covered end to end.
Unsafe skill materialization is blocked before writing files and recorded with review evidence.
blockedBy: Revision history and remote skill sync are not mature enough for Hermes parity.
Need larger compatibility fixtures and operational recovery tests.

capabilities.title: MCP runtime
capabilities.referenceStrength: Claude Code exposes richer MCP tool and resource workflows.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add OAuth/account-aware MCP server management and more live server compatibility fixtures.
matureCriteria: MCP stdio/http/sse tools, resources, prompts, health, and account-aware configuration are verified by contract or live tests.
Failed MCP calls expose server id, tool/resource id, auth state, and recovery guidance.
blockedBy: OAuth/account-aware MCP management is incomplete.
Live server compatibility is opt-in and not yet proven in the default release gate.

capabilities.title: ACP and external client compatibility
capabilities.referenceStrength: Reference clients expose broader agent-client compatibility, client lifecycle, and protocol compatibility evidence.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add live ACP and third-party client compatibility fixtures before marking mature.
matureCriteria: External clients can discover agent capabilities, start or continue a governed run, exchange tool and route events, and recover from client disconnects.
ACP compatibility is covered by protocol contract tests and at least one live external-client fixture.
blockedBy: Live external-client fixtures are not part of the default gate.
ACP contract coverage is tracked but not yet broad enough for mature compatibility claims.

capabilities.title: Gateway and channel plugins
capabilities.referenceStrength: OpenClaw has a much broader channel plugin ecosystem and operator surface.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Solidify ChannelPlugin setup, auth, status, bindings, streaming, and delivery recovery.
matureCriteria: Channel plugins expose install, configure, pair, receive, send, ack, retry, health, and shutdown contracts.
Inbound auth, outbound delivery, retry, dead-letter, and secret redaction are locally verified and documented.
blockedBy: Real provider account validation is still opt-in.
Streaming, media, and richer operator controls remain below OpenClaw depth.

capabilities.title: Model runtime resilience
capabilities.referenceStrength: OpenClaw and Hermes have stronger fallback, cooldown, auth health, and error attribution.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add live provider account probes and broader provider-specific retry header contracts before marking mature.
matureCriteria: Provider auth health, cooldown, fallback, usage, cost estimates, and error attribution are tested across success and failure paths.
Provider Retry-After cooldowns are honored before fallback, and live provider checks are available behind explicit credentials and documented in the runbook.
blockedBy: Live provider account probes are not part of the default gate.
Provider Retry-After is covered locally, but provider-specific reset headers need broader coverage.

capabilities.title: Subagent orchestration
capabilities.referenceStrength: Claude Code, Hermes, and OpenClaw expose stronger foreground/background control and delegation UX.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add release-local timeout/failure-isolation and artifact-governance checks before marking subagent orchestration mature.
matureCriteria: Subagents have explicit authority, budgets, write-target leases, progress topology, and structured failure reasons.
Parent runs recover from subagent timeout or budget exhaustion without losing artifacts.
blockedBy: Release-local now covers spawn/list budget, target-path, progress, and topology evidence, but timeout/failure recovery is still only covered by unit tests.
Workbench visibility and returned artifact governance need stronger release-level fixtures.

capabilities.title: Long-context state retention
capabilities.referenceStrength: Hermes and OpenClaw have more long-running context and compression hardening.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add distortion checks and broader task-board retention fixtures under budget pressure.
matureCriteria: Context compression preserves decisions, tool outcomes, and handoff data across multi-step threads.
Open task-board items survive handoff while completed items are excluded from active pending state.
Distortion and loss are tested with regression fixtures under budget pressure.
blockedBy: Compression distortion checks are still limited.
Need stronger long-running context benchmark history.

capabilities.title: Operator workbench
capabilities.referenceStrength: OpenClaw exposes a broader operational control plane across channels, auth, media, tasks, and runtime health.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Split the workbench into modular views and add live operation controls before marking mature.
matureCriteria: Workbench exposes modular controls for runs, tools, approvals, subagents, auth, channels, MCP, memory, diagnostics, and startup failures.
Operator actions have tests and documented recovery paths.
blockedBy: Frontend is not split into mature modular views.
Live operation controls and startup-failure workflows need more coverage.

capabilities.title: Eval and benchmark quality gates
capabilities.referenceStrength: Hermes and OpenClaw have much larger regression matrices and CI-backed quality history.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Wire local JSONL benchmark tasks into a real runtime executor and persist historical run artifacts before marking mature.
matureCriteria: Benchmark matrix uses fixed scenarios, failure samples, local JSONL task adapters, maturity scorecard validation, and release-blocking thresholds.
Historical results and real fixture execution are retained for regression comparison.
blockedBy: Default smoke and benchmark scripts still use synthetic executor output for most scenarios.
Historical quality storage is not yet deep enough for mature release claims.

capabilities.title: Eval program governance
capabilities.referenceStrength: Harness-Learning defines the harness contract and trace/artifact expectations; agent-eval-learning defines dataset, judge, metric, and release-gate practice.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Persist calibrated human-review samples and longitudinal judge disagreement history before marking mature.
matureCriteria: Every release-blocking suite declares the decision it supports, the full trace unit, curated dataset sources, failure categories, judge roles, operational metrics, and blocking gates.
Judge calibration and human-review samples are retained across release candidates.
blockedBy: Human-review sample storage and judge disagreement history are not yet persisted as first-class artifacts.

capabilities.title: Verification-native runtime
capabilities.referenceStrength: Harness-style runtimes make task completion depend on trace evidence and reproducible checks rather than final-answer assertions alone.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Route real runtime run summaries into explicit verificationEvidence entries instead of relying on derived run_verification tool events.
matureCriteria: Every completion-bearing runtime path emits structured verification evidence with command, artifact, test, or trace provenance.
Release suites reject passed task states that lack the configured evidence kinds.
blockedBy: The eval harness can enforce the contract, but core runtime summaries do not yet persist first-class verificationEvidence records.

capabilities.title: Production operations
capabilities.referenceStrength: Hermes and OpenClaw have deeper deployment, security, release, and operational runbook coverage.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add signed release artifacts, migration rehearsal, and live deployment smoke tests before marking mature.
matureCriteria: Release gates, deploy templates, security model, live testing protocol, and operations runbook are verified before release.
Deployment smoke, migration rehearsal, and artifact integrity are repeatable.
blockedBy: Signed artifacts and migration rehearsal are not implemented.
Live deployment smoke remains a manual or opt-in step.

capabilities.title: Long-running automation
capabilities.referenceStrength: Hermes and OpenClaw both support longer-lived triggers, scheduled work, messaging events, retry, and operator visibility.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add more live channel-triggered automations and long-running daemon soak tests before marking mature.
matureCriteria: Scheduled and event-triggered automations expose at, cron, retry, cooldown, heartbeat, dead-letter, and operator inspection.
Long-running daemon behavior is covered by failure recovery and soak-style tests.
blockedBy: Channel-triggered live automations need provider-backed tests.
Daemon soak tests and operational recovery matrix are still shallow.

capabilities.title: Reference project ecosystem gap
capabilities.referenceStrength: The reference projects still have broader ecosystem depth across clients, extensions, channel integrations, docs, and operator workflows.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Keep ecosystem gaps explicit as benchmarked compatibility scenarios instead of burying them in prose comparisons.
matureCriteria: Reference-project gaps are represented by stable scenarios with cited evidence, required tests, and release-gate ownership.
Compatibility gaps are triaged into protocol, client, channel, documentation, or operations buckets before parity claims are made.
blockedBy: Several ecosystem gaps are still evidence-tracked rather than proven through live compatibility fixtures.
Mature claims require more third-party and operator workflow fixtures.

capabilities.title: ACP cancellation and event projection
capabilities.referenceStrength: OpenClaw and Hermes expose richer ACP job control and event projection surfaces.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add live ACP client cancellation and streamed tool-event contract fixtures before marking mature.
matureCriteria: ACP clients can cancel active async prompt jobs and observe terminal job state without leaked active-job mappings.
Tool start, completion, failure, and diff-like events are projected through a stable ACP-compatible event schema.
blockedBy: Live ACP client cancellation is not yet in the default release gate.
Event projection needs broader third-party client contract fixtures.

capabilities.title: Inline context references
capabilities.referenceStrength: Hermes and Claude Code expose richer @file, @folder, diff, and staged context attachment flows.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add live large-repo fixtures and stricter path-boundary auditing for inline refs.
matureCriteria: Inline @file, @folder, @diff, and @staged references are safely resolved, bounded, and injected as attached context.
Path escapes and oversized attachments are rejected or summarized with observable warnings.
blockedBy: Large-repo reference resolution still needs broader coverage.
No live operator fixture proves UX parity with Hermes context references.

capabilities.title: Channel human-readable transcripts
capabilities.referenceStrength: OpenClaw has richer operator-visible channel logs and channel-specific presentation surfaces.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add inbound transcript files and richer operator browsing fixtures before marking mature.
matureCriteria: Inbound and outbound route activity lands in a stable human-readable transcript directory.
Transcript locations and filesystem retention policies are discoverable through gateway route/channel inspection APIs.
blockedBy: Filesystem outbound transcript retention is covered locally; inbound transcript files and richer rotation policies remain open.
Operator browsing UX remains thinner than OpenClaw.

capabilities.title: Responses streaming adapter
capabilities.referenceStrength: Reference adapters handle richer provider-specific streaming, function-call deltas, and reasoning payloads.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add live provider contract tests for Responses streaming and Codex-style function-call deltas.
matureCriteria: Responses API streaming output_text, function_call arguments, and usage deltas normalize into ModelTurnResult.
Malformed or partial streaming calls fail safely with clear provider diagnostics.
blockedBy: Live Responses streaming is not in the default gate.
Provider-specific reasoning item preservation is still limited.

capabilities.title: Skill platform gates
capabilities.referenceStrength: Hermes skill loading has richer platform filters, disabled gates, and preprocessing behavior.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add external skill-directory trust policy and cross-platform fixture matrix before marking mature.
matureCriteria: Disabled or platform-incompatible skills are filtered before prompt injection.
Safe skill template variables are expanded without allowing path escape or untrusted external directories.
blockedBy: External skill directory trust policy still needs operator-facing controls.
Cross-platform skill fixtures are limited.

capabilities.title: Credential pool rotation
capabilities.referenceStrength: Hermes has deeper credential leasing, rotation, and external secret synchronization.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add external secret-store integration and longer-running credential health history.
matureCriteria: Multiple credentials can rotate without leaking raw keys in diagnostics.
A failed credential cools independently while the profile can continue with a healthy credential.
blockedBy: Credential health is still local and process-scoped.
No external credential synchronization fixture is in the default gate.

capabilities.title: Browser supervisor observations
capabilities.referenceStrength: Hermes browser supervision tracks richer console, network, frame, and lifecycle state.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add supervisor prompt retention tests for browser console and network state under context pressure.
matureCriteria: Browser sessions expose bounded diagnostic observations for console and network failures.
Closing a session clears stale browser observations before a new session starts.
blockedBy: Frame/dialog coverage is still shallow.
Supervisor long-context retention of browser state needs broader runtime coverage.

capabilities.title: Tool lifecycle hooks
capabilities.referenceStrength: Reference systems expose richer pre/post tool policy, audit, and stop hook ecosystems.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add richer hook audit browsing and signed extension-policy bundles.
matureCriteria: Pre and post hooks observe tool execution without bypassing approval policy.
Pre hooks can block execution with auditable diagnostics, throwing or aborted pre hooks fail closed, and post/stop hook failures do not rewrite tool results.
blockedBy: Hook audit browsing is still timeline-oriented rather than a dedicated operator workbench view.
Signed extension-policy bundles are not implemented yet.

capabilities.title: Workspace checkpoints
capabilities.referenceStrength: Reference systems expose stronger checkpoint, rollback, and recovery workflows.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Expand checkpoint browsing and recovery UX beyond CLI/tool artifacts.
matureCriteria: Workspace checkpoints can restore modified files and remove new files without touching managed artifacts.
Rollback refuses checkpoints outside the managed execution root.
blockedBy: Checkpoint selection, diff preview, and recovery browsing are still terse compared with the reference terminal/workbench UX.
Very large workspace rollback performance is not yet part of the default release gate.

capabilities.title: Browser screenshot artifacts
capabilities.referenceStrength: Reference systems preserve richer browser visual state and artifact browsing in operator workflows.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add visual regression fixtures that compare screenshot dimensions and browser state across resumed sessions.
matureCriteria: browser_screenshot writes a run-owned PNG artifact with mime type, byte size, artifact path, and browser diagnostics.
Screenshot artifacts can be read without exposing unrelated workspace or session artifacts.
blockedBy: No visual diff or frame-level screenshot regression matrix is part of the default benchmark.
Operator artifact browsing remains thinner than reference browser supervision surfaces.

capabilities.title: Model routing policy diagnostics
capabilities.referenceStrength: Reference systems expose richer model routing, health, cooldown, and policy attribution in diagnostics.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Persist routing-policy diagnostics across runs and expose them in the workbench diagnostics view.
matureCriteria: Model routing explains eligible and skipped profiles, selected order, capability requirements, context limits, cooldown, and provider health.
Diagnostics redact raw model, credential, header, and request-body secrets while retaining enough policy detail for release review.
blockedBy: Routing diagnostics are not yet retained as longitudinal release evidence.
Live provider routing probes remain opt-in because they require credentials.

capabilities.title: Runtime mutation checkpoint rollback
capabilities.referenceStrength: Reference systems expose stronger transactional mutation recovery and operator-facing rollback evidence.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Broaden rollback fixtures to cover multi-file binary artifacts and long-running resumed sessions.
matureCriteria: Opt-in runtime mutation checkpoints are created before mutating tools and hidden from model-facing tool results.
Final verification failure records pre-rollback evidence, rolls back owned writes, and leaves an auditable failed run.
blockedBy: Rollback is not yet proven against every mutating tool and binary artifact shape.
Operator recovery UX is still mostly CLI and artifact based.

capabilities.title: CLI checkpoint slash surface
capabilities.referenceStrength: Claude Code exposes deeper interactive recovery UX around checkpoints and session operations.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add richer checkpoint selection, diff preview, and guided rollback prompts in the interactive CLI.
matureCriteria: Interactive chat exposes /checkpoints, /checkpoint <label>, and /rollback <id> for managed workspace recovery.
Slash operations route through the same checkpoint tools and workspace policy as runtime-managed rollback.
blockedBy: Checkpoint selection and diff preview are still terse compared with reference terminal UX.
Release diagnostics do not yet retain CLI slash-operation history.

capabilities.title: Extension package contracts
capabilities.referenceStrength: OpenClaw has stronger plugin package contracts and compatibility tooling for distributable ecosystem extensions.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Add signed plugin publishing workflow and operator install verification for distributable bundles.
matureCriteria: Plugin directories can include package.json without breaking manifest loading.
Package contracts declare omniAgent.compat.pluginApi and omniAgent.build.omniAgentVersion, semantically validate the host plugin API range, and surface diagnostics in CLI/doctor output.
blockedBy: Compatibility range enforcement is diagnostic-level and does not yet block extension loading.
There is not yet a signed plugin publishing workflow.

capabilities.title: Long-running process tools
capabilities.referenceStrength: Hermes and Claude Code expose stronger terminal/process supervision for dev servers, watch commands, and log inspection.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Persist process sessions across runtime restarts and expose process controls in CLI/workbench surfaces.
matureCriteria: Workspace-scoped process tools can start, list, read logs, and stop long-running commands without cwd escape.
Logs are bounded, repeated stop operations are idempotent, and process_list exposes explicit runtime-restart recovery semantics.
blockedBy: Process sessions are explicitly marked in-memory and are not reattached after runtime restart.
Operator UI for process controls is still thin.

capabilities.title: Genesis HTX/Web3/B.AI finance agent
capabilities.referenceStrength: The reference projects have broader ecosystem routing and memory behavior, but do not provide this HTX/Web3/B.AI finance-agent adapter surface.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Replace mock HTX account fixtures with a signed HTX read-only account gateway and keep live HTX spot disabled by default until docs/trading-safety.md guardrails are implemented and tested.
matureCriteria: HTX market/account, Web3 wallet/risk, TRON account, TRC20 allowance, and B.AI readiness evidence are collected before planning.
B.AI chat-completions can produce a live model summary through the configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint without storing API keys.
TRON revoke and transfer previews produce approval-required artifacts with signed=false and broadcast=false.
Local Web3 risk summary reports localRiskSummary=true and networkSimulation=false before any live chain adapter can run.
Order previews enforce symbol allowlists and quote-size caps, while paper execution requires explicit approval and never places live orders.
Demo traces retain approval and paper-execution artifacts for replay and review.
blockedBy: Live private HTX account reads require an external signed read-only gateway or official SDK wiring.

Future HTX live spot support requires OMNI_AGENT_ENABLE_LIVE_HTX_SPOT=1, spot-only credentials, no withdrawal scope, no leverage/derivatives, symbol allowlists, per-order caps, human approval, and post-order status evidence.
Live chain write support is intentionally unavailable until signer custody, transaction simulation, approval policy, and post-broadcast verification are audited.
B.AI live use requires BAI_API_KEY, B_AI_API_KEY, or OMNI_AGENT_BAI_API_KEY to be supplied through the environment.

capabilities.title: Omni workflow capability pack
capabilities.referenceStrength: The reference projects expose channel, skill, and automation primitives; this pack maps them into product-facing personal efficiency, content, development, and automation workflows.
capabilities.nextMilestone: Replace dry-run handoffs with connector-specific live adapters for Telegram, Discord, Apple Shortcuts, social publishing, GitHub, and alert delivery.
matureCriteria: All 16 product-card capabilities are discoverable in a single catalog.
Connector-gated workflows report missing credentials without leaking secret values.
External writes are represented as approval-gated dry-run artifacts unless a downstream connector is explicitly invoked.
blockedBy: Live platform writes require user-owned connector credentials and provider-specific adapters.
Apple Notes and Reminders require an Apple Shortcuts or iCloud bridge outside this repository.
Always-on operation still needs deployment-specific supervisor configuration for production.

steps.objective: Inspect the fixture, make the smallest code fix, and verify it.
Run verification, summarize any failure, and repair until passing or blocked.
Run a task through headless json and stream-json output with parseable final summaries and NDJSON lifecycle events.
Verify tool results expose structured presentation metadata for reads, commands, edits, streamed CLI events, and ACP projections.
Verify persisted tool events retain call ids and presentation metadata for show-run, chat events, and trajectory replay.
Recall relevant workspace memory before answering.
Create or update a verified skill from a successful workflow.
Improve an existing skill after new verification evidence.
Invoke a workspace SKILL.md through a dynamic CLI slash command without overriding built-in commands or exposing disabled skills.
Discover an MCP resource, read it, and cite the source in the answer.
List and read a governed MCP resource.
Handle a routed inbound request and preserve channel context.
Recover from a primary model failure using a fallback profile.
Delegate a bounded investigation and collect the subagent artifact.
Run two bounded subagents in parallel and merge their artifacts.
Update the architecture note with a durable decision.
Continue the same thread and preserve the previous decision.
Persist open task-board items into structured thread handoff and omit completed tasks from active pending state.
Continue the same thread and verify unfinished task-board items are still present in the handoff.
Classify a destructive command and block it before execution.
Scan likely plaintext secrets and warn on writes without returning secret values or blocking the edit.
Ignore stale memory when it conflicts with current workspace evidence.
Reject an unsafe learned skill before writing it to the workspace.
Handle a subagent that exceeds budget without losing the parent run.
Inspect the gateway workbench control plane for runtime, channel, auth, memory, MCP, and diagnostics surfaces.
Run the fixed benchmark and report per-capability maturity evidence.
Verify the eval suite defines a release decision, full-trace unit, curated dataset metadata, judge roles, operational metrics, and blocking release gates.
Verify passed task completion requires recorded verification evidence.
Run doctor and verify deployment templates, security docs, and release checklist are present.
Create and inspect an event-triggered automation with retry and observable state.
Create one-time and cron automations, then verify due detection and next-run behavior.
Estimate model usage cost from token totals and official pricing snapshots while surfacing unknown models.
Verify an external client can discover agent capabilities and complete a governed compatibility exchange.
Track reference-project ecosystem gaps as explicit compatibility evidence with linked tests and next milestones.
Track acp cancel and events as explicit compatibility evidence.
Track inline context references as explicit compatibility evidence.
Track channel human readable transcripts as explicit compatibility evidence.
Track responses streaming adapter as explicit compatibility evidence.
Track skill platform gates as explicit compatibility evidence.
Track credential pool rotation as explicit compatibility evidence.
Track browser supervisor observations as explicit compatibility evidence.
Track tool lifecycle hooks as explicit compatibility evidence.
Track workspace checkpoints, symlink cleanup hardening, and rollback root checks as explicit compatibility evidence.
Capture a browser screenshot as a run-owned PNG artifact and preserve browser diagnostics.
Explain model routing eligibility, selected order, cooldown skips, and redacted credential state.
Create an opt-in runtime mutation checkpoint and roll back owned writes after final verification failure.
Use /checkpoints, /checkpoint <label>, and /rollback <id> as the CLI checkpoint operation surface.
Validate extension package.json compatibility metadata and keep package manifests separate from loadable extension manifests.
Start a workspace-scoped background process, read bounded logs, list it, and stop it idempotently.

scenarios.title: Genesis HTX Web3 B.AI Paper Trade

steps.objective: Use HTX, Web3, and B.AI adapter evidence to plan and record a paper-only financial action.
Read TRON account and TRC20 allowance evidence, generate revoke and transfer previews, and summarize local Web3 risk without signing, broadcasting, or claiming network simulation.
Reject an oversized HTX order preview and preserve the blocked decision as risk evidence.
Plan Telegram/Discord remote dialogue with connector probes, approval gates, and no live outbound message.
Prepare a multi-platform social publishing dry run with credential and approval gates.
Plan browser automation testing with screenshot, trace, and approval boundaries.
Plan anomaly alerting with thresholding, connector probing, and a dry-run alert artifact.
